subtitulo: Put destination, purchase, validation, transfer and boarding in the correct order
introPt: A traveller needs local transport to the Historic Centre. Listen for the two different destination checks and the two obligations discovered in between.
cenario: At a staffed terminal, the traveller buys a ticket, validates it and boards the correct bus after one transfer.

dialogo.es: Sí, pero tiene que hacer transbordo.
dialogo.pinyin: see, PEH-roh TYEH-neh keh ah-SEHR trahns-BOR-doh
dialogo.pt: Yes, but you have to transfer.

dialogo.es: Un boleto para el centro, por favor. ¿Tengo que validar el boleto?
dialogo.pinyin: oon boh-LEH-toh PAH-rah el SEHN-troh por fah-BOR. TEHN-goh keh bah-lee-DAHR el boh-LEH-toh
dialogo.pt: One ticket downtown, please. Do I have to validate it?

dialogo.pinyin: EHS-teh ow-toh-BOOS bah al SEHN-troh ees-TOH-ree-koh
dialogo.pt: Does this bus go to the Historic Centre?

perguntas.pergunta: Why ask the destination before buying?
perguntas.explica: The first destination check ensures the product being bought serves the journey.

perguntas.pergunta: Which ticket word does the Mexican SKU teach?
perguntas.explica: Boleto is the working Mexican travel-ticket word used here.
Validar and hacer transbordo occupy the action slot.

perguntas.pergunta: Why confirm the bus again at the door?
opcoes: The first question protected purchase; this one protects boarding
perguntas.explica: The same destination closes a different risk at the vehicle.

perguntas.pergunta: How should a difficult line or platform number be handled?
opcoes: Show or read it from the display
perguntas.explica: Numbers stay on the surface; pointing and reading are the permitted escape hatch.
